the combination of plasmonic perforated gold films and TiO2 adhesion films leads to a synergistic enhancement of the electrochemical hydrogen evolution reaction.

the development of a new generation of plasmonic photocathodes with enhanced electrochemical activity for the hydrogen evolution process, which could be of great interest for the development of future energy technologies.
the development of a new class of plasmonic electrocatalysts for hydrogen evolution, which can be used in tandem with plasmonic water splitting photocatalysts.
the use of plasmonic nanostructured gold thin films for the electrocatalysis of the hydrogen evolution reaction under light irradiation and the importance of the adhesion layer.

plasmonic electrodes can be used as a new class of efficient hydrogen production catalysts, and the use of plasmonic materials in electrocatalysis is a promising strategy to enhance the performance of electrocatalytic systems.
the TiO2 adhesion film plays an essential role to enhance the electrocatalysis of the perforated gold thin layer.

plasmonically enhanced hot electrons are a viable strategy for improving the electrocatalysis of water splitting.

plasmonic electrodes are promising candidates for the electrochemical production of H 2, and the Ti/Ti O 2 adhesion layer plays a crucial role for the plasmon induced hot electrons injection into the underlying semiconductor, which is the key for the enhancement of hydrogen evolution reaction.

plasmonics is a powerful approach for the electrocatalysis of water splitting.
